tools.name: import_score
tools.description: Open as a draft a score the person gives whole: a .cesure file's text, AlphaTex, or an "Open in Cesure" link. The score is taken as it is, never rewritten.

tools.name: read_score
tools.description: Read measures from..to of a track of the draft (all by default, 200 at most a call: past them, the answer's more says where to go on) as .cesure measures — id, time signature, voices in the compact notation (second voice, hands, ties included) — with the repeat signs and tempo changes of those measu

tools.name: edit_measures
tools.description: Rewrite measures from..to (numbers, inclusive) of ONE track of the draft with .cesure measures, as read_score returns them; to = from - 1 inserts before from. Keep the id of each measure you keep, even rewritten: a measure written without its id is a new measure, and the one it stood for is removed

tools.name: transpose
tools.description: Shift the notes of the draft by some semitones; the placement follows. A note no string of its track can carry once shifted stays where it was: the answer counts them (notesLeftInPlace).

tools.name: refinger
tools.description: Place the notes of the draft again on the neck (string and fret), keeping their pitches: mode auto, standard (lowest frets) or optimized (fewest hand moves); searchCapo lets it choose a capo.

tools.name: undo_last_change
tools.description: Give the draft back the score it held before its last change (edit_measures, transpose, refinger, or an undo): the score it holds now becomes the one before, so calling it again redoes. One step only, and only when Cesure had room to keep that score; it says so when it had not.

tools.name: search_catalog
tools.description: Search Cesure's catalog of free pieces by title or composer; returns title, artist, licence and link.

tools.name: open_in_cesure
tools.description: Show the draft in the Cesure player, to read and hear it: call it once the score is ready. Where the host draws apps, the player plays the draft in the conversation; everywhere, the answer gives the short link that opens it in Cesure, with no account, and the score's summary.

tools.name: list_my_scores
tools.description: The scores of the person's linked Cesure account ("My scores"), most recently changed first, 200 a call (offset skips the first ones; when there are more, the answer's more gives the next offset): id, title, when last changed, and its tags; then every tag of the account, with how many scores carry i

tools.name: read_my_score
tools.description: Open one score of the linked account as a draft, by the id list_my_scores gives: the answer is the draft and the score's summary; read_score reads its measures. Needs the account linked.

tools.name: save_new_score
tools.description: Save the draft as a NEW score in the linked account's library (never overwrites one; a free account keeps 3 scores), under a title (default the score's own). Needs the account linked.

tools.name: update_my_score
tools.description: Write the draft back over the score of the linked account's library it was opened from (read_my_score), as saving in the app does: refused, nothing overwritten, when the score was saved in Cesure since. The library keeps the score's earlier version. Needs the account linked.

tools.name: organize_my_scores
tools.description: Organize the scores of the linked account with tags, in ONE batch applied whole or not at all (at most 500 changes, counting the tags add creates): create_tags creates tags, add puts a tag on a score (creating the tag if the account has none of that name; names compare without case), remove takes it
